resolution: Closed in round 2 by commit d54ab12 (lib/resolve-swap-identity.mjs + bin/spawn-funding-swap.mjs rewrite) and round-2's rewritten CRIT-006, re-independently-verified again in round 3's verdict.json: expectedBaseSignerAddress/sourceBaseAddress are now sourced EXCLUSIVELY from resolveOwnBaseIdentity()'s ANICCA_HOME-gated, viem-derived value (bin/spawn-funding-swap.mjs:70-71) -- no SPAWN_FUNDING_SWAP_EXPECTED_BASE_SIGNER_ADDRESS/SOURCE_BASE_ADDRESS env read exists anywhere in the feature's production code. This finding is retained verbatim below for audit-trail purposes only and is NO LONGER a blocking finding as of round 2/3 (see reviews/contracts/sprint-1/output/verdict.json, blockingFindings: []).
description: CRIT-006's description claims: 'the ground-truth mechanism is an explicit pinned-parameter gate on deps.akashKeyName/deps.expectedBaseSignerAddress, not a literal process.env.ANICCA_HOME read... identity is pinned via explicit caller-supplied parameters, never resolved from shared environment state.' This is only true for deps.akashKeyName, whose required value (REQUIRED_AKASH_KEY_NAME = "anicca-akash") IS a hardcoded literal in lib/driver.mjs:28. It is FALSE for deps.expectedBaseSignerAddress: bin/spawn-funding-swap.mjs:17 sets `const EXPECTED_BASE_SIGNER_ADDRESS = process.env.SPAWN_FUNDING_SWAP_EXPECTED_BASE_SIGNER_ADDRESS;` and bin/spawn-funding-swap.mjs:47 passes that env-sourced value straight into deps.expectedBaseSignerAddress in the production wiring path (buildDeps()). So the 'pin' half of CRIT-006's identity check that is supposed to defend against loading another Anicca instance's key (NFR-5: 'no key belonging to any other Anicca instance... may be loaded... explicit gate, no shared-env fallback', behavioral-spec.md:425-436) is, in the actually-delivered bin/spawn-funding-swap.mjs, itself sourced from a process-environment variable -- exactly the class of shared-env-fallback mechanism NFR-5 exists to forbid. If SPAWN_FUNDING_SWAP_EXPECTED_BASE_SIGNER_ADDRESS is ever exported in a shell/cron context also inherited by another Anicca instance (Franklin, anicca-a3cdd4), or is simply left unset in a misconfigured deployment, the 'pin' provides none of the protection CRIT-006 and NFR-5 both claim. bin/spawn-funding-swap.mjs IS explicitly in this sprint's delivered scope (contracts/sprint-1.md's frontmatter 'scope' field and 'Files touched' list both name it), yet CRIT-006's passThreshold instructs the adversary to read ONLY lib/driver.mjs's runSwap and re-run lib/__tests__/driver-preconditions.test.mjs (which supplies expectedBaseSignerAddress as an in-test literal, never exercising bin/spawn-funding-swap.mjs's env-var-sourced production wiring at all) -- so a Phase-3 adversary following CRIT-006 verbatim would never read bin/spawn-funding-swap.mjs and would never discover that the 'pinned-parameter, never shared-env' characterization is false for expectedBaseSignerAddress in the code path that actually runs in production.
fix: Either (a) hardcode EXPECTED_BASE_SIGNER_ADDRESS as a literal constant in bin/spawn-funding-swap.mjs (mirroring driver.mjs's REQUIRED_AKASH_KEY_NAME pattern) so it is genuinely pinned and not shared-env-sourced, or (b) if an env var is kept for operational flexibility, add a CRIT/passThreshold that reads bin/spawn-funding-swap.mjs and requires a test/fixture proving that env var is never inherited from -- or collides with -- another instance's shell/cron scope, and correct CRIT-006's description to stop claiming the mechanism is 'never resolved from shared environment state' when it currently is for expectedBaseSignerAddress.
